slides.title: What is Students' Voice?
slides.content: Students' Voice is the process through which students influence: Teaching and learning. Student experience. College facilities. Equipment and software. Timetabling and support. Good student feedback can lead to real improvements when it is specific and evidence-based.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'What is Students' Voice?'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on What is Students' Voice?.

slides.title: What Makes Students' Voice Effective?
slides.content: Students' Voice works best when: Reps consult their group. Feedback is specific. Students raise issues before meetings. People follow up on agreed actions. Example: ✅ "Four edit stations cannot run Premiere." ❌ "The software is rubbish."

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'What Makes Students' Voice Effective?'? Select all that apply.
options: People follow up on agreed actions
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on What Makes Students' Voice Effective?.

slides.title: Ways to Get Involved
slides.content: There are four main ways: Student Representative: Represents your class and attends Student Council meetings. Student Governor: Represents students at Governing Board level. NUS Membership: Provides access to student benefits and discounts. Surveys and Forums: Give students another way to influence college decisions.

slides.title: What Does a Student Rep Do?
slides.content: A Student Rep: Gathers student opinions. Attends Student Council meetings. Gives feedback about teaching and facilities. Helps find solutions. Reports back to the group. Represents both the course group and English/Maths class.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'What Does a Student Rep Do?'? Select all that apply.
options: Gives feedback about teaching and facilities
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on What Does a Student Rep Do?.

slides.title: Why Become a Student Rep?
slides.content: The role develops: Communication skills. Leadership skills. Problem-solving. Professional conduct. Employability skills. These are qualities employers value.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Why Become a Student Rep?'? Select all that apply.

slides.title: What is a Student Governor?
slides.content: Student Governors: Sit on the Main Governing Board. Contribute to strategic decisions. Help shape budgets and resources. Bring a student perspective to leadership discussions. Governors are not the same as Representatives. Reps represent a specific group. Governors contribute to decisions affecting the whole college.

exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on What is a Student Governor?.

slides.title: Encourage Unity
slides.content: The featured PROUD value is: This means: Working together. Sharing concerns collectively. Supporting representatives. Improving things for everyone, not just yourself. Evidence from a group has more influence than a single complaint.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Encourage Unity'? Select all that apply.
options: Improving things for everyone, not just yourself
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Encourage Unity.

slides.title: Elections
slides.content: Each group elects: 1. A Course Representative. 2. An English/Maths Representative. Representatives must: Be elected fairly. Be registered officially. Attend required training.

slides.title: Quick Revision Summary
slides.content: Key points to remember: Understand Students' Voice Learn how representatives work Give specific, evidence-based feedback Participate in elections Support Encourage Unity Use your voice constructively
